anomalies.observed: On the THT MCU footprint U2 (ATtiny45-20P) the POT net is on physical pin 2 (PB3) and TACH on pin 3 (PB4). On the alternative SMD footprint U3 (ATtiny13V-10S) the same two nets are reversed: POT is drawn on pin 3 and TACH on pin 2, and the symbol's internal names are also swapped (it labels pin 3 as PB3 and pin 2 as PB4, contradicting the ATtiny13 datasheet where PB3=pin2, PB4=pin3).
anomalies.expected: U2 and U3 are alternative (THT vs SMD) footprints for the same MCU function and are populated one-or-the-other, so every net must land on the same physical pin on both. ATtiny13 and ATtiny45 share an identical 8-pin mapping (PB3=pin2, PB4=pin3), therefore POT should be on pin 2 and TACH on pin 3 on U3 as well, matching U2.

evidence.quote: Page 1/2: U2 'ATtiny45-20P' (THT) shows pin 2 -> POT, pin 3 -> TACH, with internal names XTAL1/PB3 at pin 2 and XTAL2/PB4 at pin 3
Page 1/2: U3 'ATtiny13V-10S' (SMD) shows pin 3 -> POT, pin 2 -> TACH, with internal names PB3 at pin 3 and PB4 at pin 2
Page 1: J3 'POT' pin 2 carries the POT net; J2 'FAN' pin 3 TACH_IN carries the TACH net (single shared nets to both MCU footprints)

anomalies.impact: If the SMD footprint U3 is populated instead of U2, the potentiometer setpoint (POT) and the fan tachometer feedback (TACH) are wired to the opposite GPIO pins (PB4 vs PB3). The firmware, written for the THT pin map, would then read the tach pulses as the speed setpoint and the pot voltage as the fan speed, so the fan controller regulates to the wrong speed and loses proper closed-loop feedback.
